subject: Records: flatten nested dicts into path columns and nest them back
brief:
Let the tabula records module handle nested records (dicts inside dicts), as JSON data often has them.

1. `from_records` and `from_jsonl` take `flatten=False` and `sep='.'`. With flatten, a value that is a non-empty dict is replaced by one entry per key, named by the path of keys joined with sep (to any depth), so an inner key b of an outer key a becomes the column a.b with the default separator. Columns keep first-seen order, nested keys appearing where their parent stood, depth first. Lists and other values are kept as single values, never spread into columns. Edge case: an empty dict has nothing to spread, so it stays the value of its own column. An explicit `columns` list names flattened columns. If two different paths in one record produce the same column name (for example a top-level key that already contains the separator), raise ValueError.
2. `to_records` and `to_jsonl` take `nest=False` and `sep='.'`, the inverse: a column whose name contains sep becomes nested dicts along the parts of its name; columns without sep stay top-level. A nested value that is None (for example one that a record lacked when the table was flattened) is written as None at its nested place. Nesting is refused with ValueError when one column name is a proper path prefix of another (a column a next to a column a.b), since a would have to hold a value and a dict at once; names that merely start with the same letters are fine. Without nest, such tables convert as before. With `drop_none` as well, None values are dropped before nesting and a nested dict is only created when it receives at least one value, so no empty dicts appear.
3. As a result, a nested JSON Lines text read with flatten and written back with nest gives the same objects, and a flattened table survives that round trip unchanged.
4. sep must be a non-empty string; otherwise raise ValueError.

All behavior that the existing tests check must keep working.
